examples.question_text: For $f(x)=(x-2)^2,\ x\ge2$ and $g(x)=2+\sqrt x$, verify both compositions and state their domains.

examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=5\left(\frac{x-4}{5}\right)+4\\&=x-4+4\\&=x\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}g(f(x))&=\frac{5x+4-4}{5}\\&=x\end{align*}$
Both compositions return $x$ for every real input, so $f$ and $g$ are inverses.

examples.question_text: Verify that $f(x)=\frac{3}{x-2}$ and $g(x)=2+\frac{3}{x}$ are inverses. State the domain of each composition.
examples.solution_text:
For $x\ne0$, $g(x)-2=\frac{3}{x}\ne0$, so $g(x)$ is an allowed input to $f$.
$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=\frac{3}{2+\frac{3}{x}-2}\\&=\frac{3}{\frac{3}{x}}\\&=x\end{align*}$
For $x\ne2$, $f(x)=\frac{3}{x-2}\ne0$, so $f(x)$ is an allowed input to $g$.
$\begin{align*}g(f(x))&=2+\frac{3}{\frac{3}{x-2}}\\&=2+(x-2)\\&=x\end{align*}$
The domain of $f(g(x))$ is $\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$; the domain of $g(f(x))$ is $\mathbb R\setminus\{2\}$. Both compositions return their input on these domains.

$\begin{align*}f(2)&=6(2)+5\\&=17\end{align*}$
The inverse undoes adding $5$, then multiplying by $6$:
$f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x-5}{6}$.
$\begin{align*}f^{-1}(f(2))&=f^{-1}(17)\\&=\frac{17-5}{6}\\&=2\end{align*}$
